subject: Observability stack renewal — cost / retention tradeoffs and vendor alternatives
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 9 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Observability stack renewal — cost / retention tradeoffs and vendor alternatives

Team —

Quick summary: our Datadog subscription renews in early Feb and Grafana Cloud/Sentry add-ons line up in Q1. Financial run-rate for logs + tracing has crept up ~32% year-over-year; retention add-ons (hot/warm tiers) are the largest driver.

Goals for this thread:
- Decide whether we pursue consolidation (Datadog full platform) vs split (Grafana for metrics/dashboards + Sentry for errors + cheaper long-term log retention)
- Identify 1–2 negotiable levers (retention window, index vs archive, commit term)
- Assign who owns vendor push / procurement entry

Notes from initial ops review (attached spreadsheet):
- Peak ingestion patterns show a high tail during deployments; average token/volume down but spikes matter for pricing buckets.
- We can aggressively compress and adjust log retention to 7/30/90-day tiers on lower-value logs. Some product teams need 365-day for audit traces.

Options I'd like us to surface:
A) Consolidate to Datadog with a retention add-on discount and committed ingestion cap (single vendor simplicity, likely higher sticker but ops ease)
B) Move to hybrid: Grafana Cloud for metrics/dashboards, Sentry for errors, and a low-cost cold store (S3-based) for long tail logs with a small hot window in vendor UI
C) Re-bid the entire stack with 12-month vs 36-month term scenarios and ask for retention credits in exchange for extended commit

Quick asks: can each of you take an option and outline pros/cons + estimated delta vs current spend by Monday EOD? Rishi — if you can start a procurement RFx and pull previous SLA language that would be helpful.

Attachments: Grafana cost comparison (spreadsheet), Datadog usage export CSV.

Thanks —
Karthik
Director, GTM Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Maya Shah <maya@datadog.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 9 Jan 2027 13:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observability stack renewal — cost / retention tradeoffs and vendor alternatives

Hi Karthik —

Thanks for the note and the details. Appreciate the transparency on usage patterns — that helps a lot. A few datapoints from our end:
- For customers with similar profiles we typically recommend a committed ingestion cap + dynamic burst buffer to avoid egress surprises.
- We can offer a retention add-on discount tiered by committed MIB/day and a migration credit for historical cold logs if Redwood commits to a 24–36 month term.

I've attached a preliminary quote (Datadog_quote_Q1_2027.pdf) that shows three scenarios: 12m (no migration credit), 24m (5% retention credit), 36m (10% retention credit + one-time onboarding credit).

Pricing caveats:
- Indexing rules matter — we recommend using processing pipelines to drop high-cardinality fields and keep ingestion lower-cost.
- Audit data requested for 365-day retention could be provisioned to an archive tier (S3) and linked via Log Rehydration if needed — that avoids keeping everything hot.

If it helps, I can set up a short call next week with our account engineering to walk the tradeoffs (25–30 minutes).

Best,
Maya
Enterprise Account Executive, Datadog

[attachment: Datadog_quote_Q1_2027.pdf]
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Shah <maya@datadog.com>, Oliver Grant <oliver@grafanacloud.com>, Hannah Chu <hannah@sentry.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observability stack renewal — cost / retention tradeoffs and vendor alternatives

Folks — looping procurement and inviting pricing transparency across vendors. We're evaluating both consolidation and hybrid models. A couple of asks to make the apples-to-apples comparison easier: 

1) Can each vendor provide:
   - 12/24/36 month committed pricing for (a) core platform (metrics/traces/logs) and (b) retention add-on tiers (30/90/365)
   - Any migration, ingestion smoothing, or onboarding credits available for a multi-year commit
   - SLA language around data durability and role-based access logging (we need auditable logs for SOC2)

2) Specific technical constraints:
   - How log rehydration from cold store works and whether queries are transparent in dashboards
   - Limits on daily ingestion spikes and how burst protection is handled

3) Deadline: please provide formal quotes and redlines by COB Friday 2027-01-15. We'll then run an internal comparison table and decide on negotiation targets.

We will share a single RFx document in Drive (link below) — please drop quotes there and include any standard contract redlines.

Related links: https://drive.redwood.co/obs/rdw-observability-2027

Thanks,
Rishi
Head of Procurement (interim)
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observability stack renewal — cost / retention tradeoffs and vendor alternatives

Appreciate the quick turnaround and Maya's preliminary quote. Team notes after reviewing: 

- Jordan (metrics lead): leans hybrid (Option B) — Grafana Cloud gives us the dashboarding flexibility and avoids paying Datadog for features we already run in-house.
- Laura (platform ops): prefers consolidation (Option A) for reduced operational overhead but wants stronger retention credits and an ingress smoothing SLA if we go that route.
- Procurement (Rishi): wants to run the RFx and push for migration/onboarding credits tied to 24/36 month commits.

Immediate next steps (owners):
- Rishi: create the RFx in Drive and notify vendors (target: 2027-01-12 AM) — assigned.
- Jordan: sketch the technical baseline for what logs must remain hot vs moved to cold store (target: 2027-01-13) — assigned.
- Laura: schedule an ops review call with Maya/Datadog account eng + Grafana rep to dig into ingestion smoothing details (target: 2027-01-14) — assigned.

I'll consolidate vendor quotes and produce a short pros/cons + spreadsheet for executive review on 2027-01-18. If procurement can secure written migration credits in the 24–36 month proposals that will likely be the deciding factor.

Thanks everyone — short calls only, please.

Karthik
Director, GTM Operations
Redwood Inference
